newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra plays to strengths with Fincantieri.
newsitem.headline: Metra plays to strengths with Fincantieri.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra is playing to its strengths in merging its diesel engine operations with those of Italian Fincantieri, Finnish share analysts said on Thursday.
Metra Oy Ab said earlier it had tentatively agreed to merge its Wartsila Diesel unit with Fincantieri's diesel acitivities, creating the largest firm in its field.
"The company is growing its operations in a field which it does best," said Jari Vayrynen at Protos Stockbrokers.
"After the merger, diesel operations will be more strongly the number one domain for Metra," said Jukka Linden at Opstock.
After the deal, diesel operations will make up roughly 80 percent of Metra's 11 billion markka annual sales, which also include bathroom ceramics and speciality steel products.

Analysts saw clear synergies in the planned deal, particularly in product development but also in marketing and sales; and said it should enable Metra to boost its market share in diesel maintenance, which would help boost profit margins.
"Metra has the best knowledge on maintenance, it could be expected that it would expand its market share," Vayrynen said. "That would have a leverage effect on earnings," he added.
Metra so far is unique in having a worldwide maintenance network for its engines -- maintenance currently accounts for one third of Wartsila Diesel's 6.9 billion markka turnover.
The first step would be for the Finnish company to take up maintenance of Fincantieri's 50-percent owned New Sulzer Diesel engines, analysts said.
Combining with Fincantieri's diesel operations could help Metra boost benefits on product development -- which so far has absorbed some 250 to 300 million markka annually, analysts said.
In the longer term, the merger was seen having a positive impact on Metra's profits: Metra said it would not affect 1996-97 results and have a neutral impact on 1997 EPS.
Analysts welcomed this news, noting that acquisition can be a very expensive route to market share.
The new company will be part of Metra, and state-controlled shipbuilder Fincantieri will have up to a 15 percent holding in the merged company.
